bib.title: The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond
bib.venue: Foundations and Trends in Information Retrieval, Vol. 3, No. 4, pp. 333-389

question: How is the Probabilistic Relevance Framework developed from the probability ranking principle into BM25, BM25F and related ranking functions, and how are their parameters set?
contributions: Conceptual derivation of PRF from the PRP to sum-of-weights scoring (Sec 2)
Derived models: BIM/RSJ, relevance feedback, eliteness model, BM25, BM25F, non-textual features, positions (Sec 3)
Comparison with Maron-Kuhns, unified model, language models, topic models and DFR (Sec 4)

limits: Not an experimental survey: performance statements derive from many uncited experiments (Sec 1).
Binary, document-independent relevance and term independence are assumed and 'arguable' (Sec 2.2, 2.4.2).
Model gives no guidance on setting k1 and b (Sec 3.5).
Dropping rank-irrelevant terms means no calibrated probability of relevance, which hurts blind feedback and filtering (Sec 2.5, 3.3).
Positional information is not a natural PRF extension (Sec 3.8).
IDF for BM25F streams left as open research (Sec 3.6.3).
practices: Use k1 about 1.2-2 and b about 0.5-0.8 as starting values, then tune on judged queries (Sec 3.5).
Without relevance information use the idf form of the RSJ weight (Sec 3.1).
For fielded documents sum weighted, length-normalised tf over streams first and saturate once per term (BM25F, Sec 3.6.1, 3.6.3).
Tune on a grid with caching; tune k1,b first, then stream weights, then k1 and b_s (Sec 5.1, 5.2.1).
Expand queries with the top ~10 offer-weight terms (Sec 3.2).

terms.definition: If retrieved documents are ordered by decreasing probability of relevance on the data available, then the system's effectiveness is the best that can be obtained for the data.
A hidden binary document-term property, a form of aboutness; term frequency depends on eliteness, which is associated with relevance.
Any one term's contribution to the document score cannot exceed a saturation point (the asymptotic limit).
BM25 extension to weighted streams: accumulate stream-weighted, length-normalised tf per term, then saturate.
